one_line_contribution: A token- and format-matched control the agentic-memory literature never runs: replacing per-query retrieved experience with decoys, with a single dev-selected fixed prefix, or with an offline-compiled instruction, and showing accuracy is statistically unchanged while the agent still demonstrably imitates the injected items — i.e., the read channel's query-conditioning, not just its volume, is inert.
closest_prior_work: Atlas (arXiv:2603.15666) is the nearest and the proposal is right that it builds the replacement (compile experience into the system prompt) without showing the replaced channel contributed zero; the residual delta is therefore a single contrast, correct-vs-decoy/fixed-prefix at matched tokens. The under-treated threat is Dynamic Cheatsheet (arXiv:2504.07952), which already runs one persistent cross-query artifact against per-item retrieval; the proposal dismisses it in one clause ('presented as a method with its own gains') without saying whether its ablations already include a token-comparable per-query-retrieval arm — if they do, prediction 4 is largely pre-empted and only predictions 1-3 survive. arXiv:2505.16067 further shows retrieved experience is often followed and sometimes harmful, so 'retrieval does not help' is already partly on the record; what is new is only 'correct is worth no more than decoy at matched tokens, with following held high'.
strongest_objection: The decisive grid is centred on A1(7), a budget the proposal's own research track already measured as net harmful (7 retrieved items fixed zero and broke six to seven, McNemar p=0.031/0.016; cutting to three eliminated the harm). If A1(7) is at or below A0, then A1(7)-A2(7) and A1(7)-A3(7) are equivalence tests between two treatments that do not work, and prediction 1's '>=80% of whatever advantage correct retrieval holds over A0 survives' is undefined rather than confirmed. The one arm at the budget where retrieval plausibly helps, A1(3), is demoted to the 1-seed supporting set and has no matched counterparts — there is no A2(3) and no A3(3) — so the central claim cannot be evaluated at k=3 at all. Compounding this, the environments are chosen where a query-independent prior is near-sufficient by construction (WebShop's action grammar and ALFWorld's task templates are shared across queries; a decoy from a 'different task family' still demonstrates search[...]/click[Buy Now]), so a null is close to a foregone conclusion and does not license the general claim that query-conditioning is inert. The design's own guard against that triviality — A5 (oracle nearest-gold) and A2u — sits in the 1-seed supporting tier with no null replicate, i.e. the arms that decide whether the headline is a real finding or 'our bank had no exploitable content' are the least powered arms in the paper. Risk factor 5 names this exact failure and then does not resource it.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Make A1(k*) - A0 > equivalence margin a stated gate, exactly parallel to the ExpeL fidelity gate: if correct retrieval does not beat no-memory by more than +/-3 reward points, report that and stop, because every downstream equivalence claim is vacuous. (2) Run the full conditioning triplet at both budgets — A1(3)/A2(3)/A3(3) as well as k=7 — with 2 seeds each, so the claim is not confined to a budget already known to be over-injected. (3) Promote A5 and A2u into the decisive set with null replicates; a flat oracle should be reported as 'bank had no headroom', not as support for inertness. (4) Add one environment where the bank contains information not recoverable from the query itself (site-specific quirks, tool-schema exceptions, cross-episode facts) so that a bank with demonstrated conditioning headroom exists somewhere in the paper; without it the title claim outruns the evidence. (5) Fix the offline-compute arithmetic: '~20 iterations against a 300-episode dev split' totalling 3,300 dev episodes across 11 GEPA runs implies ~15 episodes per candidate evaluation, far below the paper's own 5-14 point re-scoring drift, so P2's 'plateau' curve cannot distinguish convergence from noise and predictions 4-5 inherit that.
missing_baseline: A sham/counterfactual following-rate baseline: score A0 (no-memory) episodes against the items that would have been retrieved, using the identical n-gram/entity/LLM-judge pipeline. Prediction 3 — the dissociation that the abstract calls the core evidence — is uninterpretable without it, because in WebShop and ALFWorld the action vocabulary is tiny and correct items share entity strings with the query, so 'following' is measured with an upward bias on A1 and a downward bias on A2/A3; a decoy following rate at 70% of the correct rate could be entirely chance overlap, and equally a low decoy rate could be metric artifact rather than the agent ignoring the text. Secondary omission: a random (not dev-selected) fixed prefix. A3(7) is chosen by a search over the bank for highest mean dev retrieval score, while A1(7)'s only dev tuning is scalar k*; a null A1-A3 is therefore partly explained by A3 being an optimized baseline rather than by conditioning being inert, and a random-7 arm would separate 'format alone suffices' from 'dev-selected items suffice'.
preprint_collision: The check is above average in form — nine queries, two named material collisions, an explicit scoop-exposure statement for Atlas, and a gap statement scoped as a claim about the search rather than proof of absence. It is undermined by its own audit trail: it reports that a previous round's citations (MemHarness 2607.28272, RecMem 2605.16045, AtomicRAG 2604.20844, Distractor-Aware Truncation 2608.03297, and 'Decocted Experience' 2604.04373, previously called the closest threat) could not be re-found, and that arXiv:2606.06036 appeared in the prior round under a different title. The same identifier carrying two titles across rounds is evidence that part of the reference set is confabulated, and the author further concedes Atlas's venue and authorship could not be verified beyond a returned introduction. Since novelty here rests entirely on 'no one runs this control', an unverifiable corpus is a substantive weakness, not a neutral: the two papers most likely to already contain a version of the control (Dynamic Cheatsheet 2504.07952, which maintains one shared cheatsheet, and ExpeL's own published insights-vs-trajectories ablation) are dismissed in a sentence each without reporting what their ablation tables actually contain at matched token budget. I would require the collision check to be re-run against verifiable listings and to state, per candidate, whether a fixed-set-vs-per-query arm at equal tokens exists.
